answer: Ferrous anchor escrow: each new agent identity must lock a small hardware-attested token whose private key is bound to one physical device; only that device can sign the agent's first N transactions. The issuer cross-checks the device serial against a shared ocean of prior registrations, so a clone must acquire and register fresh hardware rather than copying keys. Cloning one identity costs a real device plus its registration latency, while the original earns the same yield as the meadow of honest agents—making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
